change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 restriction that hides website
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so it is omitted when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, i.e. for TL0 users seen by anonymous. `website_name` is a new attribute (line 43) and is not in that list. For such a user the JSON now carries `website_name` but no `website`. The old controller computed `websiteName` from `model.website`, so nothing was shown. The template now renders the globe icon and the host name (user.hbs:66-71) from `model.website_name`. The `href` and `title` are empty, so it shows as a dead link. This also exposes the host and path of a link the restriction exists to hide, which defeats the anti-spam purpose. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`. That helper already defines an `include_website_name?` that checks `.present?`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` so it is never called
findings.body: The serializer convention in this file is `include_<attr>?` (for example `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, and the methods that `untrusted_attributes` and `staff_attributes` define). `include_website_name` without `?` is dead code. `website_name` is therefore always serialized, as `nil` when there is no website, instead of being omitted. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or drop it and rely on `untrusted_attributes`. If you keep a custom method, it must also keep the restricted-user check from the previous finding. A `def` placed after the `untrusted_attributes` call would otherwise override the helper's version.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic is wrong for multi-part public suffixes and is hard to read
findings.body: The same-length branch compares everything after the first label. `foo.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk` (both 3 labels) have equal tails (`co.uk`). An unrelated site on the same public suffix is then shown with its full path, although the intent is only to do that for the same registrable domain. The three branches also call `URI(website.to_s)` up to twice and repeat `split('.')`. Parse once into a local and extract the helper. The `"." << website_host` on line 149 is a mutating idiom. Prefer `".#{website_host}"` or `end_with?`. Also, a bare `http://example.com/` returns `example.com/` with a trailing slash.

findings.title: Missing coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch, blank or invalid websites, and restricted users
findings.body: The three new examples cover only the `else` branch (different domain) and the `website_host == discourse_host` and `ends_with?` cases. They do not cover the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` against `forum.example.com`, line 144-146), a website with no scheme or an unparseable URL (returns nil), or a blank website. They also do not cover the TL0-user-seen-by-anonymous case, where `website` is omitted. The last of these would have caught the leak of `website_name`.

contracts.action: Profile page renders website name from server-provided website_name instead of computing it client-side
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed controller computed property websiteName (split('/')[2] of model.website) in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6
contracts.before_after: Before: the client derived the host from model.website, so a user with a hidden website (restricted TL0 viewed by anonymous) showed nothing. After: the server computes website_name, but it is not covered by untrusted_attributes, so it is sent even when website is omitted.
contracts.visible_effect: Globe icon and host text appear for restricted users with an empty href/title. For allowed users, the host (or host plus path) shows as intended.
contracts.failure_mode: A malformed website makes URI parsing raise, which is rescued to nil, so website_name is nil and the block is hidden. No error is shown.

summary: The change moves website-name computation to the serializer. The new `website_name` attribute is not in `untrusted_attributes`, so it leaks the hidden website of restricted TL0 users and renders a dead link. `include_website_name` lacks the `?` and is never called. The branch heuristic and the specs have smaller gaps.
